# Decisions made by the builder

Calls the design left open, made under charter section 3. Newest last.

| Id | Date | Decision | Reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| B-001 | 2026-11-13 | Tests live in `backend/tests/<module>/`, mirroring `backend/src/shifde/<module>/`; shared helpers in `backend/tests/_support/`; schema tests in `backend/tests/schema/`. Run one module with `uv run pytest tests/<module>`. | Keeps the installed package free of tests while staying "beside the module" one directory over; design §8 leaves layout to the builder. |
| B-002 | 2026-11-13 | Local PostgreSQL 17 cluster on port 55450, data in `.devdata/pg/`, managed by `python scripts/dev_db.py init|start|stop|status`. | Must not collide with SETH's 55440 (design §8). A Python script works from both PowerShell and bash. |
| B-003 | 2026-11-13 | Roles keep SETH's names: `shifde_owner` (owns schema, runs migrations) and `shifde_app` (NOSUPERUSER, NOBYPASSRLS, owns nothing). | Ported SQL and policies refer to these names; renaming adds churn for no gain. |
| B-004 | 2026-11-13 | One Alembic `versions/` directory; root revision `base_0001` (branch label `base`); each module's revisions carry `branch_labels=("<module>",)` and `depends_on` the modules whose tables they reference. Upgrades use `alembic upgrade heads`. | Lets modules be built in parallel without revision collisions (design §5.4). |
| B-005 | 2026-11-13 | Schema comparison: `scripts/make_seth_schema_snapshot.py` migrates a scratch database with SETH's own migrations at `3ba0e06` (from `git archive`, SETH untouched) and writes `backend/tests/schema/seth_3ba0e06.json`; `tests/schema/test_schema_vs_seth.py` compares every ported table against it, allowing only entries listed with a reason in `backend/tests/schema/deliberate_changes.yaml`. | An automated, repeatable comparison that does not depend on SETH's dev database. |
| B-006 | 2026-11-13 | Parallel tests with pytest-xdist: migrate a template database once per run, then one `CREATE DATABASE ... TEMPLATE` per worker. | Design §6 asks for one database per worker and a 20-minute full suite. |
| B-007 | 2026-11-13 | The usage report attributes sub-projects through `docs/build/units.json` (unit → sub-project); units not listed count as `sp1`, the lead as `lead`. | Agent descriptions carry the unit, not the sub-project. |
| B-008 | 2026-11-13 | Agent files in `.claude/agents/` load only when a session starts, so in the session that created them each role runs as `general-purpose` with the charter's model for that role, told to read and follow its role file; the description ends with `(role)` and the usage report attributes it to that role. | Keeps model choice fixed by the charter and token attribution by role, without waiting for a new session. |
| B-009 | 2026-11-13 | Hosted database steps are held: no roles created, no migrations run there. Everything is proven on the local cluster (charter §2 fallback). | Checked 2026-11-13 with the supplied `DATABASE_URL` (contents not printed): the server is PostgreSQL 16.13, not 17, and refuses TLS (`sslmode=require` → "server does not support SSL"); the design (§3, §5.4) requires TLS. Creating role passwords and running the application over cleartext to a public address would break that requirement. The named database `truss_harness` is empty (0 tables) and would be this project's database once TLS is available; no `seth_unified` database is needed. The connecting role is a superuser on a server holding about 25 other databases, which were not touched. |
| B-010 | 2026-11-13 | Module builders take their own source inventory as their first step; `scout` is used only for summaries that come back as text (e.g. long failing output). | Subagents in this environment may not write report files, so a scout inventory would pass through the lead's context and then again into the builder's: more tokens for the same information. |
| S-001 | 2026-11-13 | Charter section 10 (context size, handoff, spending less) and `scripts/context_size.py` added by the supervising session; from session 2 on, the build runs in headless sessions that supervising process starts, without the owner's connectors (`--strict-mcp-config`) and with automatic compaction off. | The owner asked the supervising session directly on 2026-11-13 to own context management (hand off instead of automatic compaction) and model cost. Measured: starting context about 40k tokens per session or agent without the connectors, against about 73k with them. |
| B-101 | 2026-11-13 | Backend `pyproject.toml` is SETH 3ba0e06's verbatim (ruff, mypy strict, pytest, all five import-linter contracts) with two changes: dev deps `pytest-xdist` and `filelock` added; entry points for modules not yet ported (`shifde-admin`, `shifde-worker`, all `shifde.adapters` entry points) removed, to be re-added by the port that brings each module. `python-dotenv` is not added: it is already a dependency of `pydantic-settings` and SETH's `core/settings.py` uses it the same way. | An entry point naming a missing module breaks the install; filelock guards the once-per-run template migration under xdist. |
| B-102 | 2026-11-13 | Every module name SETH's import-linter contracts mention exists as a placeholder whose only content is the docstring `Not yet ported from SETH 3ba0e06; see docs/build/STATUS.md.` (top-level modules as packages, submodules as `.py` files or packages exactly as in SETH). Contracts are unchanged. | `lint-imports` errors on a contract that names a missing module; ports overwrite the placeholders. |
| B-103 | 2026-11-13 | 15 placeholders carry one import besides the docstring: `<m>.service` imports `<m>.repository` (models_admin, audit, identity, connections, runtime, governance, build, ontology, tenancy, secrets, vendors) and `<m>.repository` imports `<m>.models` (audit, identity, tenancy, secrets). | import-linter 2.15 fails a contract whose `ignore_imports` entry matches no import (`unmatched_ignore_imports_alerting` defaults to `error`). The only other fix is changing that setting, i.e. the contract configuration, which the charter forbids. The real service/repository modules make the same imports, so the ports replace these lines naturally. |
| B-104 | 2026-11-13 | The baseline `base_0001` keeps SETH's names for the per-transaction context: settings `app.tenant_id`, `app.principal_id`, `app.platform_admin`, read by `shifde.current_tenant_id()`, `shifde.current_principal_id()`, `shifde.is_platform_admin_ctx()` (fail closed on unset). It also holds the shared trigger helpers `shifde.set_updated_at()` and `shifde.reject_mutation()`, schema `USAGE` and `alembic_version` `SELECT` for `shifde_app`. The plan's `shifde_current_org()`/`app.org_id` is not used; organization = tenant = client. The tenancy port's migration must not re-create these five functions. | SETH's policies and `core/db.py` use these names; renaming them would touch every ported policy and the schema comparison. |
| B-105 | 2026-11-13 | No `ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES` in the baseline. | SETH grants each table explicitly and minimally (no DELETE anywhere, column-level UPDATE); a default grant would widen privileges on every new table and show up as a difference in the schema comparison. |
| B-106 | 2026-11-13 | SETH's tables live in schema `shifde`, not `public`. `test_rls_schema.py` therefore checks every table in every non-system schema (`shifde` and `public`, excluding only `shifde.alembic_version`; see B-112); `global_tables.txt`, `ported_tables.txt` and the snapshot use bare table names in schema `shifde`. | Checking only `public` would check nothing; checking every schema means a table created in the wrong schema still cannot escape the rule. |
| B-107 | 2026-11-13 | The role check (`shifde.core.dbrole.check_app_role`) refuses, for the session role and every role it is a member of (`pg_has_role(..., 'MEMBER')`): superuser, BYPASSRLS, REPLICATION, CREATEROLE, owner of the database, of any non-system schema (includes `public`), relation or function, CREATE privilege on any non-system, non-temporary schema (including through PUBLIC) or on the current database, and the predefined `pg_read_server_files` / `pg_write_server_files` / `pg_execute_server_program` / `pg_read_all_stats` / `pg_monitor` / `pg_read_all_data` / `pg_write_all_data` / `pg_maintain` roles. It also refuses a fresh connection on which `app.tenant_id`, `app.principal_id` or `app.platform_admin` is already set (role or database `SET`, URL `options`, `PGOPTIONS`, `postgresql.conf`) and any `pg_db_role_setting` row setting `app.*` for the session role, the database or all roles. It runs in `Database.__init__` (so `create_app` and every later entrypoint, the worker included, are covered; `verify_role=False` only for owner tooling such as the `owner_db` test fixture) and again in `shifde-api`'s `run()`, which exits 3 with one line on stderr before binding, also when the role cannot be checked (fail closed). Isolation review 1, items 3, 4, 5, 7; review 2, items 9, 10. | Owning a function such as `current_tenant_id()` or a schema is as good as owning the tables; server file access reads table files around RLS; REPLICATION streams every row; CREATEROLE can grant itself the owner role on PostgreSQL 15 and earlier; statistics roles see other sessions' query texts; CREATE in a schema or the database lets the role shadow names (a schema named after the role is first on the default `"$user"` path); the all-data roles hold every grant this codebase withholds; a preset context turns fail-closed helpers into a fixed client or platform admin. |
| B-108 | 2026-11-13 | Local cluster: one cluster for all checkouts, data and secrets in the main checkout (`.devdata/pg`, `.devdata/cluster.env`), superuser `postgres`, `max_connections = 600`; each checkout gets database `shifde` (main) or `shifde_<worktree>` and its own `.devdata/dev.env` (variable names as SETH). `dev_db.py start` also ensures roles, the checkout's database and its dev.env. `shifde_owner` keeps SETH's attributes (BYPASSRLS, CREATEROLE). | One cluster per machine is cheaper than one per worktree; 600 connections because `pytest -n auto` starts 96 workers on this machine. |
| B-109 | 2026-11-13 | Test harness: databases `shifdet_<run>_tmpl` (migrated once under a file lock, then marked `IS_TEMPLATE`, `ALLOW_CONNECTIONS false`) and `shifdet_<run>_<worker>`; the xdist controller drops whatever the run left. Per-test cleanup truncates the tables modules register in `tests/conftest.py:CLEAN_TABLES` (none yet, so unit tests need no database). Test directories are packages (`__init__.py`) so module folders can share file names such as `test_cross_client.py`. | Fast, xdist-safe, and leaves no databases behind. |
| B-110 | 2026-11-13 | Schema snapshot per table: columns, constraints (keyed by name: type and definition), indexes, triggers, RLS enabled/forced, policies, and table/column privileges of `shifde_app`. Functions are not compared. A `deliberate_changes.yaml` entry whose path does not differ, or whose table is not in `ported_tables.txt`, fails the test. | Triggers carry SETH's append-only and immutability guards; constraint names matter to error mapping in SETH code; stale exceptions should not linger. |
| B-111 | 2026-11-13 | `shifde.core.migrations.code_heads()` added beside SETH's verbatim `code_head()` (which raises once there are several branch heads); the core port switches the readiness check to it. The skeleton serves `GET /healthz`; SETH's `/api/health` arrives with the observability port. A test downgrades the worker database to `base` and upgrades it to every head, so every migration's `downgrade()` is exercised. | B-004 gives one head per module branch. |
| B-112 | 2026-11-13 | `test_rls_schema.py` checks relations of kind `r`, `p`, `v`, `m`, `f` in every non-system schema; only `shifde.alembic_version` is exempt. Tables need forced RLS, a policy, and every PERMISSIVE policy tenant-keyed: USING (ALL/SELECT/UPDATE/DELETE) and an explicit WITH CHECK (ALL/INSERT/UPDATE) must reference `shifde.current_tenant_id()` or `shifde.current_principal_id()` and be built from recognised forms: `<key column> = helper` or `NOT (<key column> IS DISTINCT FROM helper)` (either side), where `KEY_COLUMNS` ties `current_tenant_id()` to `tenant_id` (+ `shifde.tenants.id`) and `current_principal_id()` to `user_id` (+ `shifde.users.id`); `shifde.is_platform_admin_ctx()`; and bare `tenant_id IS NULL` only in the USING of a FOR SELECT policy (in every WITH CHECK and in the USING of ALL/UPDATE/DELETE, each occurrence must sit in an AND with `shifde.is_platform_admin_ctx()` as a direct conjunct; review 3, items 3, 4). On a relation with a `tenant_id` column only tenant atoms count, in USING and WITH CHECK (`tenant_id` keyed to `current_tenant_id()`, the admin flag, the shared-rows atom): a principal key may narrow in an AND but not satisfy (review 4, item 1); principal keys count only on relations without `tenant_id`, and a bare principal key (`user_id`) only on a relation listed in the reviewed `PRINCIPAL_TABLES` (schema-qualified name -> reason), seeded with `shifde.sessions`, `shifde.local_credentials`, `shifde.user_identities` (per-person identity state, not client content); `shifde.users` keeps its table-specific `KEY_COLUMNS` key without a listing (review 5, item 1). A `PRINCIPAL_TABLES` entry is stale and fails unless it names a table without `tenant_id` that has a permissive policy keyed to `current_principal_id()` in the database under test, or a SETH 3ba0e06 principal-keyed table not yet in `ported_tables.txt`; adding an entry needs isolation review. OR needs every branch recognised, AND at least one conjunct. `EXISTS` subqueries and anything else pass only as an exact-text entry of `REVIEWED_EXPRESSIONS` keyed (relation, policy, command, PERMISSIVE/RESTRICTIVE, roles, clause) (review 3, item 6), which fails on any change and on a stale entry. Every policy expression, RESTRICTIVE included, goes through the context-write scan (B-117); beyond it a RESTRICTIVE policy is not constrained (it can only narrow). No rewrite rules on any relation except a view's or materialized view's `_RETURN`. Views need `security_invoker=true`; materialized views and foreign tables must be in `global_tables.txt`. Expressions are read under `search_path = pg_catalog`. | Isolation review 1, items 1, 2, 11; review 2, items 1, 2, 3, 11; review 3, items 2, 3, 4, 6; review 4, item 1; review 5, items 1, 2 (a principal key separates people, not clients: a staff user in several clients wrote content in client B and read it in client A through an unlisted `own_row` table; review 5, item 2 adds the principal wrong-column probe on a listed table without `tenant_id`). Explicit WITH CHECK is stricter than PostgreSQL (which reuses USING) so the write rule is always written out and reviewed; rule actions run as the owner (BYPASSRLS). SETH 3ba0e06 policies this rejects, to be resolved by their ports with isolation review: `USING (true)` on `adapter_conformance_runs`, `installation_profile`, `installation_settings`, `permissions`, `run_state_transitions`, `workers` (candidates for `global_tables.txt`); `installation_settings.write_platform_admin` (admin flag only); `audit_events.write_own` WITH CHECK `tenant_id = current_tenant_id() OR tenant_id IS NULL` (audit port: any client could write a global audit row; still the only SETH policy the review 3 shared-row rule rejects; the review 4 tenant-atom rule rejects no further SETH policy, both checked against the snapshot); `users.users_insert` WITH CHECK `... OR current_tenant_id() IS NOT NULL` and `users.users_select` USING with the membership `EXISTS` (identity port: rewrite or add to `REVIEWED_EXPRESSIONS`). |
| B-113 | 2026-11-13 | `base_0001`'s helpers call builtins schema-qualified (`pg_catalog.current_setting`, `::pg_catalog.uuid`, `OPERATOR(pg_catalog.=)`, `pg_catalog.now()`), use `CASE` instead of SETH's `NULLIF` (which resolves `=` through the search path), and have no `SET search_path` clause. `test_function_schema.py` pins the five helpers by oid (each the one zero-argument function of its name in `shifde`; a second function with the name fails, review 3 item 5; owner, not SECURITY DEFINER, no SET clause, language, volatility, return type, body) and requires every SECURITY DEFINER function in every non-system schema to be on `SECURITY_DEFINER_ALLOWLIST` (`<schema>.<name>`) with a reason, pin a `search_path` without `public`/`$user` and with `pg_temp` last, and grant EXECUTE only to its owner and `shifde_app`. | Isolation review 1, items 7, 8; review 2, items 4, 6, 7. Unlisted, `pg_temp` is searched first. A SET clause would stop PostgreSQL inlining the SQL helpers into every policy; a definer function owned by `shifde_owner` bypasses RLS. |
| B-114 | 2026-11-13 | `Database` registers a pool `checkout` hook: `DISCARD ALL` (review 2, item 8: also drops temporary objects, prepared statements, `SET ROLE`, `LISTEN`; SETH keeps no session state across a checkout, and psycopg clears its prepared-statement cache on `DISCARD ALL`), then refuse (raise `UnsafeDatabaseRole`, which makes SQLAlchemy discard the connection) if any of the three `app.*` context settings is set. | Isolation review 1, items 4, 6: session-level settings a previous user left are wiped; a preset that survives `RESET ALL` comes from the role, database, options or server and is refused on every checkout. Connection `options` (timezone=UTC) survive `DISCARD ALL`. `shifde_app` keeps TEMPORARY on the database (SETH grants it); temporary objects cannot outlive a checkout. Savepoint desync of `set_tenant` inside `begin_nested()` stays with the `core`/`tenancy` ports. |
| B-115 | 2026-11-13 | `Settings.effective_migration_url` raises `MigrationUrlMissing` when `SHIFDE_MIGRATION_DATABASE_URL` is unset (SETH fell back to `SHIFDE_DATABASE_URL`). `dev_db.ensure_roles` revokes every membership of `shifde_app`, per grantor. | Isolation review 1, item 13: migrations never run as the application role; `shifde_app` is a member of no role. |
| B-116 | 2026-11-13 | Isolation review 1 items deferred to their owning units: **9** (TRUNCATE ignores RLS) -- the schema test must assert `shifde_app` has no TRUNCATE, TRIGGER or REFERENCES on client tables, FKs between client tables are composite `(tenant_id, id)`, and unique constraints on client tables include `tenant_id`; owner: the schema test, extended by each module port as its tables arrive (first: `tenancy`). **10** (design 5.3) -- policies on client-content tables must not OR `shifde.is_platform_admin_ctx()`, only platform catalogs may; owner: `tenancy` (and isolation review of every port). **12** -- every cross-client test asserts `current_user = 'shifde_app'`; owner: every module port (shared helper in `tests/_support/` from `tenancy`). **6, savepoint part** -- `set_tenant` inside `begin_nested()` then rolled back desyncs `session.info` from the database; owner: `core`/`tenancy`. Isolation review 3: **7** -- item 9 above, plus plain FKs are checked as the owner without RLS (an FK existence check and `ON DELETE CASCADE`/`SET NULL` reach another client's rows); must land with tenancy's first client table; owner: `tenancy`. **8** (optional) -- require `tenant_id`/`user_id` on client tables to be `uuid`; owner: `tenancy`. The round 3 observation (a principal-keyed policy does not constrain `tenant_id`) is closed by review 4, item 1 (B-112). Review 4, item 3: items 7, 9 and 10 above remain tracked; owner: `tenancy`. Review 4, item 4: `rate_card_versions_guard` (B-117); owner: governance. Review 5, item 3: `sessions.active_tenant_id` is a client pointer outside the `tenant_id` rule, writable by its owner under `own_row`, and SETH 3ba0e06 `identity/service.py` turns it into `Principal.tenant_id`; the port must check the pin against the user's current bindings on every request before setting `app.tenant_id`, with a cross-client test for a revoked binding; owner: identity, tenancy. Review 5, item 4: items 7, 9, 10 above and `rate_card_versions_guard` remain tracked. | Isolation review 2, item 5; review 3, items 7, 8; review 4, items 3, 4; review 5, items 3, 4: each deferred item named with its owner so it is not lost. |
| B-117 | 2026-11-13 | Nothing in the catalog may write the client context. `tests/schema/catalog_scan.py` (`context_write_violations`, used by `test_function_schema.py` for every object kind and by `test_rls_schema.py` for policies) reads, in every non-system schema, function bodies (`prosrc` or the SQL-standard body), SET clauses and argument defaults; view and materialized-view definitions; every policy expression (USING and WITH CHECK, permissive and restrictive); column defaults and generation expressions; domain defaults; every constraint; index expressions and predicates; trigger definitions (WHEN, arguments); extended statistics; aggregates (the schema-qualified names of all support functions and `agginitval`/`aggminitval`; review 4, item 2). It fails any that mentions `set_config`, `pg_settings` or `app.tenant_id|principal_id|platform_admin` (any case, spacing or quoting, also with comments removed), or calls a builtin that runs a query given as text (`query_to_xml*`, `ts_stat`, `ts_rewrite`); in function bodies also `EXECUTE` and `U&` escapes, and functions in a language other than sql/plpgsql/c/internal. Exempt: the three context helpers, by oid. `CONTEXT_WRITE_ALLOWLIST` (label -> reason, stale entries fail) is empty. SETH 3ba0e06 code this will reject, to be resolved by its port with isolation review: `shifde.rate_card_versions_guard()` (governance, p08_0001 and p08_0003) calls `set_config('shifde.ratecard_close', ...)` (allowlist entry or a different signal). No SETH 3ba0e06 policy, view or other function is affected. | Isolation review 3, items 1, 2: a plain function, a view or a policy conjunct calling `set_config('app.platform_admin', 'on', true)` returned another client's rows; dynamic SQL and escapes would hide the names, so they are refused in bodies too. |
| B-201 | 2026-11-13 | Core port: the client address is resolved in `shifde.core.ratelimit.resolve_client_ip` and used by `get_request_ctx`. `X-Forwarded-For` is believed only when the TCP peer is in `SHIFDE_TRUSTED_PROXIES` or is loopback (the same-host frontend proxy); the chain is read right to left, first untrusted address wins, a malformed hop falls back to the peer. The default `trusted_proxies` stays `[]` (SETH tests pin it). `ip_limit_applies` is unchanged, so a direct loopback caller is still exempt but a forwarded client is limited. | Audit Item 3 (ARCH M9, SEC Major-2). The `app` port must not add uvicorn's `ProxyHeadersMiddleware` on top for loopback and must have the frontend proxy append (not replace) `X-Forwarded-For`. |
| B-202 | 2026-11-13 | Core adds `core/bodylimit.MaxBodySizeMiddleware` (pure ASGI, 413 problem+json, counts streamed bytes) and settings `max_request_body_bytes` (8 MiB, 0 = off); `SlidingWindowLimiter` takes a `message`. Not yet wired: the `app` port adds the middleware, the `identity` port uses the limiter for API-key failures and the OIDC callback. | Audit Item 5b core part. |
| B-203 | 2026-11-13 | `Database(connect_timeout=10, statement_timeout_ms=0)` set libpq `connect_timeout` and a startup `statement_timeout` (survives the checkout `DISCARD ALL`). Settings `db_connect_timeout_seconds=10`, `db_statement_timeout_ms=60000`; the API/worker constructors (later ports) pass them, owner tooling keeps 0. `core.health.migration_state` compares the set of database revisions with `code_heads()` (B-111); `db.read_db_revisions` added. | Audit Item 18 (core part; `/api/ready` and worker wiring remain known defects 18/19). |
| B-204 | 2026-11-13 | `repr()`/`str()` of `Settings` print `database_url` and `migration_database_url` with the password replaced by `***`; `model_dump()` still returns them. | ARCH m1. A masking `model_dump` would break `model_copy`/round-trips used by tests. |
